How weeks are counted
×

A week runs Monday to Sunday. Complete the number of sessions you chose. Scheduled rest days do not use a session slot.

A completed week adds one. Extra sessions do not add extra streak points. A week still in progress does not end your streak.

Recovery keeps your place. A paused week protects the previous streak without adding a completed week. Resume when you are ready; your goal starts again the following week.

Your history stays yours. If a week ends below your goal, the consecutive count starts again. Your completed weeks and sessions remain.

Sleep Hygiene

Science-backed evening rituals to protect deep sleep and wake up truly restored.

The 7-Hour Foundation

Seven to eight hours of uninterrupted sleep is your single most potent performance and recovery tool.

Deep vs. REM Sleep

Deep sleep repairs physical tissue, while REM sleep processes emotional stress and sharpens focus.

Evening Wind-Down Ritual

Dim warm lighting, cooler room temperatures, and screen boundaries cue your brain for natural melatonin release.

Can You Repay Sleep Debt?

Weekend sleep-ins can slightly reduce tiredness, but circadian consistency is what truly restores vitality.

The 20-Minute Power Nap

A brief early afternoon nap refreshes cognitive sharpness without interfering with your nightly sleep drive.

Workout Essentials

Building sustainable movement habits that stick without causing burnout.

Consistency Beats Intensity

Showing up for 20 mindful minutes every day builds far greater long-term health than sporadic weekend heroics.

The Power of Variety

Blending brisk walking, bodyweight strength, and mobility keeps connective tissue supple and resilient.

Finding Your Natural Cadence

Pacing is about matching effort to how your body feels today, rather than chasing a fixed speedometer.

The Truth About 10,000 Steps

The 10k number was an arbitrary marketing metric; real health benefits begin accumulating around 6,000 steps.

Progressing Safely

Increase your weekly volume by no more than 10% to give tendons and joints time to adapt.

HEALTHY EATING
Why Good Fats Matter

Avocados, nuts, and olive oil provide steady, long-lasting energy while protecting your joints and balancing hormones.

THE SCIENCE SIMPLY PUT

Unlike quick-burning simple sugars, healthy unsaturated fats metabolize slowly, stabilizing blood glucose and keeping you satiated for hours after meals.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR YOU

Cellular membranes, brain tissue, and joint fluid rely on essential fatty acids to cushion movements and reduce systemic inflammation after exercise.

EVERYDAY PRACTICE

Add a quarter avocado, a spoonful of chia seeds, or a drizzle of cold-pressed olive oil to your meals instead of relying on ultra-processed snack bars.

💡

KEY TAKEAWAY
Healthy fats are essential fuel, not something to avoid. Focus on unprocessed, whole-food sources.
